tracks.legalName: Petition to Set Aside a Conviction Sentenced to Probation, Fine or Community Service (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 29-2264(2))
tracks.publicName: Set aside a Nebraska conviction where you were not sent to jail

controllingAuthority.summary: Where an offender was sentenced to probation, a fine or community service and has satisfactorily completed it, the sentencing court may set aside the conviction. The order nullifies the conviction and removes all civil disabilities and disqualifications imposed as a result of it, and must notify the offender to consult an attorney about firearm effects. Offence reaches any violation of state law or of a political subdivision, including felonies, misdemeanors, infractions, traffic infractions and ordinance violations. Section 29-2264(9) makes the 2018 and 2020 changes apply without regard to the date of the conviction.

exclusions: None stated in subsection (2). The four mandatory-denial grounds in § 29-2264(3)(b) are textually confined to subsection (3) petitions and must not be applied here.

waitingPeriods.condition: Satisfactory fulfilment of probation for the whole period, or discharge from probation before termination, plus payment of any fine and completion of any community service
waitingPeriods.duration: none independent of completion. There is no date gate: § 29-2264(9) applies the changes without regard to the date of conviction

The route is not composed: the petition and its proposed order are one submission by one actor to one destination, the judge's signature is outside-party completion of one form, and the notice of hearing is notice and hearing scheduling. limitations.statement: Say set aside, never expunge, clear or erase. Neb. Rev. Stat. § 29-2264(5) nullifies the conviction and removes civil disabilities and disqualifications; it does not seal, erase or remove the record, and § 29-2264(6) lists the many purposes for which the conviction still counts.

researchStructure.firstStage: A custom motion under Neb. Rev. Stat. § 29-3005, not CC 6:12, filed after completion of the sentence or juvenile disposition in the county, district or separate juvenile court of the county of conviction or adjudication. The statute distinguishes two branches that must not be collapsed: (a) a prostitution-related offense as defined in § 29-3005(1) committed while the movant was a victim of sex trafficking OR proximately caused by that status; (b) any other offense committed as a direct result of OR proximately caused by that status. No further multi-year waiting period in that section. Only the selected, fact-supported branch is pleaded; both alternatives are never printed as already true; the court makes the findings.
researchStructure.evidence: The rebuttable presumption of victim status may rest on government documentation OR on affidavits or sworn testimony from an attorney, clergy member, medical professional, trained victim-services professional, or other professional from whom the movant sought relevant assistance; official documentation is not a prerequisite; other sufficiently credible and probative evidence may be considered. The presumption concerns victim status, not every other element. On the movant's request a hearing on this motion must be held in camera and the rules of evidence do not apply to it; this authorises no promise that all filings are confidential or that the later sealing hearing follows the same rule. No unnecessarily graphic evidence is solicited and no testimony invented.
researchStructure.secondStage: After a signed trafficking-based set-aside order, an adult seeks sealing under § 29-3523(4) using CC 6:12, Motion to Seal Adult Criminal Record, Rev. 04/2024 (two pages), with companion instructions CC 6:12a Rev. 06/2024 at the non-obvious CC-6-12-a.pdf URL; the form assumes the set-aside has occurred; grounds are never all checked automatically, a charge date is never turned into a conviction date, continued public access is asserted only on the relevant fact; the second page's participant signature, contact and no-email alternative are preserved as execution fields; the court notifies the county or city attorney and schedules the matter. Juvenile adjudications use the juvenile-sealing mechanism referenced in § 29-3523(4), not the adult CC 6:12.
researchStructure.remainingNarrowRequirements: First-stage local motion service and scheduling, accepted declaration execution and any sensitive-filing protections for the actual court; the second-stage clerk-notice procedure is not copied into stage one. The repository's counsel-classification requirement (counselQuestions) stands: this research supplies the corrected law and drafting structure, not that approval.

controllingAuthority.summary: Firearm rights removed by a conviction are restored through the Board of Pardons process, and the judiciary states that the Board may grant a pardon with or without restoring gun rights. No standalone statewide restoration application exists. A set-aside does not restore firearm rights: § 29-2264(6) preserves the conviction for the firearm statute and § 29-2264(5)(c) requires the set-aside order itself to tell the participant to consult an attorney about firearm effects.

exclusions: Federal firearm disabilities, which Nebraska cannot lift.

geography.venue: No court venue. Restoration runs through the executive clemency process.

tracks.legalName: Nebraska Remedy for a Criminal History Record Created by Identity Theft (mechanism undetermined)
tracks.publicName: Clearing a Nebraska record that is not yours

controllingAuthority.summary: No Nebraska mechanism has been identified for clearing a criminal history record created by another person using the participant's identity. The controlling review records the authority for this matter as not surveyed and the matter as unresolved and out of scope. The nearest adjacent mechanism is the expungement of an arrest made in error under § 29-3523(9), but that subsection is triggered by the error of a law enforcement agency rather than by third-party impersonation, and it has not been established that it reaches an impersonation case where the agency made no mistake.

exclusions: Cases where the arresting agency itself made the error, which belong to the arrest-made-in-error route.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: Deferred because the governing mechanism is unidentified. This is the only Nebraska source slot that is a true blocker rather than a scope decision: the review records the authority as not surveyed, and targeted checking did not establish a statute, an agency, a vehicle, a destination or a geographic scope. Assigning any output strategy would be invention, so none is assigned and the node is unreachable. The exact evidence needed to close it is a targeted authority survey of the Nebraska identity-theft provisions, the State Patrol criminal-history correction process, the Attorney General's identity-theft materials, and whether § 29-3523(9) has been construed to reach impersonation.
